headline: Multi-omics and machine learning models nominate candidate cancer biomarkers
label: Machine Learning Transcriptomic Biomarker Discovery
summary: Recent reports integrate bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with LASSO-Cox and random survival models to nominate prognostic and therapy-response markers.
synthesis: The dominant thread is integration of bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics with machine learning to derive candidate prognostic, diagnostic, or therapy-response gene signatures. Examples include an enhancer RNA LASSO-Cox and MLP model in breast cancer, a random survival forest nominating PLPP2 as a radiotherapy-resistance biomarker in pancreatic cancer, and Cox/LASSO/random survival modeling of PPARG in osteosarcoma. Graph-attention modeling of blood multi-omics in breast cancer liver depression extends this approach to proteomic and metabolomic layers. Not all items use machine learning; several rely on network toxicology or bioinformatic screening, and a colorectal preprint contrasts CIN/CMS2 and MSI lineage states. The novelty lies mainly in multi-omic and single-cell resolution of candidate markers, though the reported findings remain hypothesis-generating.
